chunks: And as for what was narrated - Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Safwan from Al-'Iyyas ibn Al-Qasim said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who missed one night from the nights of Mina. He said, 'There is nothing upon him, and he has done well (or: he has erred).'

key_terms.لَيْسَ عَلَيْهِ شَيْءٌ: there is nothing upon him (no penalty)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a pilgrim misses a night in Mina during Hajj?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that missing a night in Mina incurs no financial penalty (kaffarah), yet the phrase 'wa qad asaa' (he has erred) indicates a spiritual or ritual shortcoming rather than a major fault. This reflects the Shia juristic distinction between obligatory acts whose omission requires compensation and those where the omission is a minor defect in the completeness of the Hajj. The hadith underscores the balance between legal ease and spiritual mindfulness in the performance of Hajj rituals.
